newsitem.title: USA: Loewen shares tumble, Service Corp. rises after bid dropped.
newsitem.headline: Loewen shares tumble, Service Corp. rises after bid dropped.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc. stock tumbled Wednesday while shares of Service Corp. International rose after Service Corp. late Tuesday dropped its $2.9 billion hostile takeover bid for its Canadian archrival.
Loewen stock fell $3.625 to $37.25 and Service Corp. rose $1.875 to $29.50, both in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Loewen had hit a high of $42.625 during the four-month takeover battle.

Service Corp. cited several factors in withdrawing its bid, including Loewen's aggressive acquisition programme, costs associated with its severance programme and uncertainties about possible divestitures needed to complete the transaction.
Houston-based Service Corp. is North America's biggest funeral home operator, ahead of Loewen, which is based in Vancouver, British Columbia.

Loewen Chief Financial Officer Paul Wagler said Tuesday that the company, an aggressive acquiror in the rapidly consolidating funeral industry, agrees with analysts' forecasts that it will do $600 million to $700 million in deals this year.
"We see that as very reasonable," Wagler said in an interview.
Separately, Service Corp.'s president said the decision to withdraw its hostile bid for Loewen will not temper his company's appetite for acquisitions.

Service Corp. plans to pursue acquisitions in Europe and elsewhere, hoping to bring in at least $200 million in new revenues, which is the amount gained from acquisitions last year, President William Heiligbrodt told Reuters.
"We've always been in the acquisition business. We're not changing any strategy," he said.
Heiligbrodt said Service Corp. would incur minimal costs from the takeover bid for Loewen, but would not elaborate.
He declined to talk about specific acquisition targets, although he said the $200 million estimate would not include a major strategic acquisition.
Other prime properties in the funeral services industry include Toronto-based Arbor Memorial Services Inc. and New Orleans-based Stewart Enterprises Inc.
Wall Street analysts said the rise in Service Corp.'s stock reflected the removal of uncertainties regarding the proposed acquisition of Loewen.
"It was prudent. The word to use is 'discipline,'" Dean Witter analyst Todd Richter said. "You've got to applaud them for not getting caught up in this and just walking away."
